title: RBACv2 gradual cutover: admin telemetry harmonization, SAML mapping, and customer communications
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Execute a low-risk, observable cutover from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with an emphasis on admin operations, unified telemetry, and stable SAML/SSO mapping. Deliverables: (1) dual-write safeback strategy + reconciliation tooling; (2) audit-log schema migration path and retention verification; (3) SAML attribute mapping validation and operator tooling for tenant-level overrides; (4) communications package for customers including opt-in/opt-out guidance and runbook snippets.
acceptance_criteria: Dual-write can be enabled for a test org with no permission regressions for 72 hours and all deltas reconciled to zero via the automated reconciler
Audit log replay for a 30-day window succeeds against RBACv2 schema with no missing critical events and parity checks show <0.01% drift
SAML mapping changes are backward compatible for existing customers; mapping translator deployed with feature flag and documented mapping table
Admin console shows a clear migration state for each org and provides a one-click rollback to v1 for orgs in the canary cohort
Customer comms templates, migration FAQ, and a public timeline published; at-risk customers identified and invited to early migration wave
tasks: Design reconciler: implement idempotent backfill worker that compares permission ledgers and emits reconciliation patches
Telemetry harmonization: tag admin actions with 'rbac_migration.v2_state' and surface in Console traces
Dual-write toggle: build safe-toggle with partial commit and audit-diff dry-run mode
SAML validator: add attribute-level validation and a stage conversion tool for common IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin)
Comms: prepare migration emails, in-console modal, and API change log entries
Runbooks: author org-level rollback and incident escalation procedures and publish to internal runbook library
comments: 2025-02-18 - Maya Chen: Kickoff completed. Agreed on low-risk approach: start with internal test orgs, then customer opt-in waves. Prioritized telemetry and reconciler before any large-scale dual-write.
2025-02-22 - Daniel Park: Prototype reconciler passes synthetic load tests (50k events/hr) but revealed ordering anomalies for near-simultaneous role deletes; added tombstone handling to worker.
2025-02-25 - Security Review (Sofia Martinez): Require audit-log parity checks and retention proof. Flagged need for encryption-at-rest proof for exported audit bundles. PKI team looped in.
2025-02-28 - UX (Priya Rao): Console migration state mockups uploaded. Must include a namespaced admin-scoped toggle and explicit warnings when rollback is unavailable.

2025-03-02 - Daniel Park: Rolled reconciler to staging for shadow orgs. Observed 0.04% mismatch on initial pass (user metadata edge cases). Patch queued to normalize email-casing and external id resolution.

notes: Trade-offs considered: immediate cutover is faster but higher-risk; this phased shadow-first approach increases engineering work but reduces customer impact.
Decision: implement reconciler-first, then enable dual-write for canary orgs with strict telemetry gates (error rate, mismatch rate, latency regression).
Fallback plan: automated rollforward that uses reconciler patches to repair divergence and an operator one-click rollback that flips traffic back to v1 routing and replays v1 audit logs to Console.
Edge cases: external SSO providers that do case-insensitive identifiers will require a migration map per-org; we've built a validation checklist for Solutions Engineers.
